greek.forms: Singular: ξένος, ξένου, ξένῳ, ξένον. Plural: ξένοι, ξένων, ξένοις, ξένους. Ionic form: ξεῖνος
greek.etymology: From PIE *ǵʰóstis 'stranger, guest'. English descendants: Xenophobia (fear of foreigners), Xenial (relating to hospitality), Xenograft (tissue transplant between species), Xenon (the 'strange' noble gas). The root appears in Latin hostis 'enemy'.
greek.usage_example: ξεῖνος δ᾽ ἐκ Τροίηθεν ἐλήλυθα — I have come as a stranger from Troy
greek.did_you_know: Greeks distinguished between three types of outsiders: ξένος (KSEH-nos) for foreign guests deserving protection, βάρβαρος (BAHR-bah-ros) for non-Greek speakers, and πολέμιος (poh-LEH-mee-os) for enemies. Breaking guest-friendship could trigger divine punishment from Zeus Xenios!
